subject: Kiribati
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Kiribati and the International Date Line. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). Island groups are shown by highlighting the country; the date line itself is not drawn.

claims.text: Kiribati’s islands, from Banaba in the west to Kiritimati in the east, straddle the equator and the 180th meridian.
Its total land area is 811 km² dispersed over 3,441,810 km² of ocean.
In 1995 Kiribati unilaterally moved the International Date Line far to the east to encompass the Line Islands group, so that the country would no longer be divided by the date line.
The move was intended to allow businesses across the expansive territory to keep the same business week.
The date line now goes around Kiribati, placing its easternmost islands in the most advanced time zone on Earth: UTC+14.
The move also enabled Kiribati to become the first country to see the dawn of the third millennium.
